etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 元 (phonetic カン) — the house finished down to the roofbeam: complete.
mnemonic: The last tile set on the roof: nothing left to build — カン. 完成! — stamp it and step back.

etymology: Compound ideograph: officials quartered (𠂤) under the state roof (宀) — government officers: the bureaucrat.
mnemonic: Under the official roof, the staff stack like sediment — カン. 警察官, 外交官: give a roof a stamp and it breeds officials.

etymology: Phono-semantic: bamboo (⺮) + 官 (phonetic カン) — the hollow bamboo tube: a pipe; what flows must be managed: control.
mnemonic: Bamboo plumbing with an official in charge of the valves — くだ. 管理: bureaucracy applied to pipes, then to everything.

etymology: Phono-semantic (simplified from 觀): 雚 'heron' (phonetic カン) + 見 'see' — the heron's fixed stare over the marsh: to observe; a view.
mnemonic: Stand heron-still and just watch — カン. 観光 is doing it on vacation; 観客 doing it in seats.

etymology: Simplified from 關: a gate (門) with its cross-bolts — the checkpoint barrier; what passes through it: connections.
mnemonic: The bolt across the gate decides who's connected to whom — カン. 関係: the doors between people; 関西: west of the barrier.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 原 (phonetic ガン) + head (頁) — the head bowed at the source of authority: to petition, to wish.
mnemonic: Head lowered all the way to the spring — ねがう. お願いします: the everyday bow this kanji performs.

etymology: Compound ideograph, classically read: four vessels (口×4) with a dog (犬) guarding them — the household's utensils; by extension, capacity.
mnemonic: Four bowls and one dog on duty between them — うつわ. 楽器, 食器: instruments and dishes, all guarded goods.

etymology: Compound: threads crossed sparse (㐅) over cloth (巾) — a weave so loose it's rare; what is rare is longed for: hope.
mnemonic: A weave with more gaps than thread: rare as the thing you're hoping for — キ. 希望: hope, honest about the odds.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 幾 (phonetic キ) — the wooden loom, the first machine; hence mechanism, and the critical moment its trigger implies.
mnemonic: The loom clacks: wood doing arithmetic — キ. 飛行機, 洗濯機, チャンスは機会 — every machine and moment descends from it.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) + child (子) — the youngest grain of the year; each round of planting: a season.
mnemonic: The grain's newest child arrives four times a year — キ. 季節: the calendar told by what's sprouting.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 義 'what is right' (phonetic ギ) — arguing out the right course: deliberation.
mnemonic: Words wrestling over what's right, at length — ギ. 会議: the room; 議論: the sport played in it.

etymology: Pictograph: a fur garment — borrowed since antiquity for 'to seek, to request' (the original sense lives on in 裘).
mnemonic: Reaching for the warm pelt in midwinter: pure wanting — もとめる. 求人: companies doing the reaching.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 立 (phonetic キュウ) — tears while standing: to weep (quietly — the loud kind is 鳴).
mnemonic: Standing still while the water runs down — なく. The kanji cries without moving; so do most adults.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 合 (phonetic キュウ) — thread supplied to match the need: to provide; what's provided monthly: salary.
mnemonic: The supply line feeds you exactly what fits — キュウ. 給料: the thread that arrives on the 25th.

etymology: Compound ideograph: water (氵) + fish (魚) — going after fish in the water: fishing.
mnemonic: Fish plus water plus intent — リョウ. A 漁師 is the fish kanji with a boat and a schedule.

etymology: Compound ideograph: two figures (立+兄) side by side, straining forward — a footrace in kanji form: to compete.
mnemonic: Twin runners frozen at the same stride — きそう. 競争 is the photo finish; 競馬 adds horses.

etymology: Pictograph: two hands raising one object together — jointly: together, shared.
mnemonic: Four hands, one load, lifted level — とも. 共通, 共同: whatever needs more hands than yours.

etymology: Compound ideograph: ten (十) + three strengths (力×3) — many muscles pulling as one: cooperation.
mnemonic: Three biceps bolted to one crossbeam — キョウ. 協力: the kanji is literally a tug-of-war team.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 亟 (phonetic キョク) — the ridgepole, highest timber of the house: the utmost point, the pole.
mnemonic: The one beam nothing sits above — きわめる. 北極 hangs the planet on it; 極めて pushes any adjective to the rafter.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 川 'stream' (phonetic クン) — teaching that flows downhill from master to pupil: instruction; the native Japanese reading 'taught onto' each kanji.
mnemonic: Words channeled like water down a course — クン. Every kanji you learn drinks from two streams: 音 and 訓.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 君 'lord' (phonetic グン) + sheep (羊) — the lord's sheep moving as one: a flock, a crowd.
mnemonic: Where the shepherd-lord walks, the wool follows in a single blob — むれ. 群馬: a whole prefecture of herds.

etymology: Compound ideograph: chariots (車) drawn into a covered ring (冖) — the encircled war-camp: army.
mnemonic: Wagons circled tight under one canopy — グン. 軍手, army gloves: the war-camp's one export to your toolbox.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 京 'capital' (phonetic ケイ) — sunlight over the capital's towers: a fine view, scenery.
mnemonic: Morning light hitting the skyline: postcard weather — ケイ. 景色 is the view; 夜景 the same city after dark.

etymology: Simplified from 藝, originally a figure kneeling to plant a seedling — the cultivated skill: art, craft, performance.
mnemonic: Planting done so precisely it counts as performance — ゲイ. 芸術 hangs in museums; 芸人 does it on television.

etymology: Pictograph: a person with mouth gaping wide — the open hole; in Japanese, what's missing: lack, absence.
mnemonic: A yawn is a hole in your face; 欠 is a hole in the roster — かける. 欠席: the empty chair kanji.

etymology: Phono-semantic: thread (糸) + 吉 (phonetic ケツ) — the auspicious knot: to tie, join, conclude.
mnemonic: Tie the lucky knot and it holds — むすぶ. 結婚 ties people; 結果 is where any thread ends up.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 建 'build' (phonetic ケン) — a person built sound and standing firm: healthy, robust.
mnemonic: A body with good architecture — ケン. 健康: the building inspection you pass by sleeping and eating well.

etymology: Phono-semantic: enclosure (囗) + 古 'old' (phonetic コ) — what has sat walled-in and aged: hardened, firm.
mnemonic: Something old sealed in a box until it sets like concrete — かたい. 固い約束: a promise past its bending date.

etymology: Compound: a person (亻) posted to watch and attend — reading the signs of sky and season: climate, symptoms, attendance.
mnemonic: The lookout notes wind, clouds, mood of the sky — コウ. 天候: the sentry's daily report; 気候: his yearly one.

etymology: Origin read as grain threshed in abundance (husks flying below the frame) — plenty, hence ease and well-being.
mnemonic: The barn full, the chaff dancing, nothing to fear from winter — コウ. 健康 pairs a sound frame with a full barn.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) over sweetness (曰) — the smell of grain cooking sweet: fragrance, incense.
mnemonic: Rice on the fire, the whole house leaning toward the pot — かおり. 香水 bottles the effect.

etymology: Compound: grain hanging uneven over the workman's square — lengths that don't match: difference, discrepancy.
mnemonic: Hold the ruler to the stalks: no two agree — さ. 時差 is the planet failing the same inspection.

etymology: Compound: a daring seizure (取) made under the helmet (曰) — the boldest stroke of all: the utmost, the most.
mnemonic: Reach in and take the top prize — もっとも, サイ. Prefix it and win any superlative: 最高, 最初, 最強.

etymology: Phono-semantic: wood (木) + 才 'inborn stuff' (phonetic ザイ) — timber with potential in it: material.
mnemonic: A log already dreaming of being a beam — ザイ. 材料 is any ingredient mid-dream; 人材 does it to people.

etymology: Phono-semantic: day (日) + 乍 'freshly cut' (phonetic サク) — the day just sliced off the calendar: yesterday.
mnemonic: The day the blade just trimmed away, still lying there — サク. 昨日: close enough to touch, gone for good.

etymology: Compound: scraping a carved block clean with cloth and blade — pressing off copies: to print.
mnemonic: Ink the block, wipe, press, repeat — する, サツ. 印刷: the wipe that filled the world's libraries.

etymology: Phono-semantic: roof (宀) + 祭 'rite' (phonetic サツ) — inspecting the rite under the roof for the smallest fault: to scrutinize, to infer.
mnemonic: Reading the ceremony for what nobody said aloud — サツ. 警察 does it for a living; 察する is doing it kindly.

etymology: Compound: wood (木) + a hook (乚) — a thin wooden slip hung up: a tag, a card; paper money by descent.
mnemonic: The wooden tag swinging on its nail — ふだ. 改札 checks yours; 千円札 is the tag you'd rather keep.

etymology: Pictograph read as hairpins glittering on a figure going to court — to present oneself: to visit (humbly), to participate; formal 'three'.
mnemonic: Dressed, pinned and sparkling: off to appear before someone — まいる. 参加 is showing up; 参りました is showing up defeated.

etymology: Compound: meat beaten apart with a stick — knocked into pieces and strewn: to scatter, disperse.
mnemonic: One whack and everything flies apart — ちる. 散歩 is the peaceful version: scattering yourself around the block.

etymology: Phono-semantic: bones (歹) + 戔 'blades' (phonetic ザン) — what the blades leave on the field: the remainder; the cruelty that left it.
mnemonic: After everything is taken, this is what stays — のこる. 残念: the leftovers of a hope.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand raised over a commanding mouth — the one who directs affairs: to administer.
mnemonic: One raised hand, one clear order — シ. 上司 gives them; 司会 directs the party with a microphone.

etymology: Simplified from 兒: an infant with the fontanelle still open (the gap in the top) on baby legs — a newborn, a child.
mnemonic: Soft-skulled and wobbling but already walking — ジ. 児童 fills classrooms; 育児 fills your nights.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 台 (phonetic ジ/チ) — mastering the rivers was the first governing; setting things right heals: to govern, to cure.
mnemonic: Tame the flood and you can rule anything, including a fever — おさめる, なおる. 政治 and 治療: same verb, different floods.

etymology: Simplified from 辭: the tongue (舌) and the branding needle (辛) — formal words, sharp enough to cut ties: an address; to resign.
mnemonic: Words with a needle in them: the farewell speech — ジ. 辞書 collects the words; 辞める uses the needle.

etymology: Pictograph: a hand with something dropping from it — gone before the fingers close: to lose.
mnemonic: The exact instant it leaves your grip — うしなう. 失敗 is losing hold of the plan; 失礼 of the manners.
